Doom's high HP pool also keeps him relatively safe from dying to Queen of Pain's high damage spells.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Bloodseeker thrives on fast movement and punishes Razor’s chase attempts with Rupture. Razor cannot run without taking massive damage. Blood Rite zones Razor from using Static Link safely. Razor gets outpaced in tempo and punished in overextensions.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Enigma can farm freely against Razor and Black Hole stops all his mobility. Razor has no disables to stop Enigma from channeling. Eye of the Storm cannot break through Black Hole without external help. Enigma’s teamfight presence overshadows Razor in big engagements.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Arc Warden’s magnetic field nullifies Razor’s physical attacks. Tempest Double can bait out Static Link and abilities. Razor cannot lock down Arc Warden long enough to prevent split-push. Arc Warden wins through patience, poke, and map pressure.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Bristleback takes reduced damage when getting hit from the back because of his passive Bristleback ability. This massively counters Riki as his Blink Strike lands him behind Bristleback for right clicks, and his Tricks of the Trade also strikes enemy units from behind in its AoE. Bristleback also releases Quill Spray or Viscous Nasal Goo from the Bristleback damage threshold, depending on the facet he selected, which reflects damage back to Riki or deters him from fighting because of the armor reduction.

pairs.name: Centaur Warrunner
pairs.reason: Centaur Warrunner's high HP gain and tanky item purchases make it extremely difficult for Riki to ever burst him down, even after he gets Diffusal Blade. Centaur's Retaliate still reflects damage inside the Smoke Screen silence to do damage back to Riki, unless he is hidden with Tricks of the Trade. If Centaur isn't the Smoke Screen target, he can use Stampede to get his teammate out of the AoE of Riki's spells and save them as Diffusal Blade does not slow movement speed during Centaur's ultimate.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Chaos Knight and his Phantasm illusions can divide the damage of Riki's Trick of the Trade and tank it together because of their high HP pool. Once a squishy Riki comes out of Tricks of the Trade, Chaos Knight and his illusions easily burst him down during the Chaos Bolt stun and Reality Rift pull. The Chaos Strike procs on right clicks from Chaos Knight still provide lifesteal and heal him up inside the Smoke Screen silence.

pairs.name: Invoker
pairs.reason: Invoker can use Tornado to dispel Escape Act.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Brewmaster can use Dispel Magic from his Storm Panda to dispel Escape Act.

pairs.name: Bloodseeker
pairs.reason: Rupture and Blood Rite take their effect despite of Escape Act's defensive properties.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Pounce and Dark Pact together with some attacks can take Rubick down quickly. Rubick's spells are ineffective due to the strong dispel effect of Dark Pact. Even though Shadow Dance is a great spell to steal, Slark's untargetable nature and his low cooldown spells prevents Rubick from stealing. Also Slark can freely use other abilities for the duration of Shadow Dance.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: Elder Titan’s aura makes Rubick extremely squishy. Rubick can’t steal any truly game-breaking spells from him, and Echo Stomp's setup often catches Rubick before he can respond. Titan thrives in chaotic fights where Rubick struggles to cast.

pairs.name: Tusk
pairs.reason: Tusk closes the gap quickly with Snowball and punishes Rubick’s weak mobility. He isolates Rubick with Walrus Punch and Ice Shards, removing him from the fight before he can react. Tusk is hard to steal anything impactful from.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Sand King relies on comboing enemies from 100 to 0 using Epicenter and Burrowstrike. However, Wraith King's Reincarnation makes him a poor target, as Sand King usually doesn't want to commit his full combo on a hero who immediately comes back to life

pairs.name: Ursa
pairs.reason: Ursa can pressure Sand King in lane because Fury Swipes deal significant damage, and as a melee hero, Sand King often struggles to trade effectively. Additionally, Ursa’s Enrage helps him mitigate much of Sand King’s combo damage, allowing Ursa to survive and stay in the fight longer

pairs.name: Oracle
pairs.reason: Oracle can consistently save allies targeted by Sand King using False Promise and Fate’s Edict, either allowing them to keep fighting or completely mitigating the burst of magical damage Sand King deals

pairs.name: Meepo
pairs.reason: A Disruption save for a teammate of SD can easily turn into set up for an enemy Meepo as he can preemptively cast Earthbind or Poof to time its duration for a chain root or massive magic damage burst. Dig can be timed to avoid Demonic Purge's or Shadow Poison's damage and effects.

pairs.name: Sand King
pairs.reason: A Disruption save for a teammate of SD can easily turn into set up for an enemy Sand King as he can preemptively cast Epicenter or Burrow Strike to time its duration for an instant stun or massive magic damage. SK doesn't really have buffs or passives for Demonic Purge to Dispel or Break, appart from Caustin Finale and Disruption doesn't stop him from doing damage with Sand Storm or Epicenter.

pairs.name: Io
pairs.reason: Io functions perfectly fine under the effects of Disruption. Io can still Relocate his allies even DURING Disruption, although Disruption would interrupt Io's Relocate if used on Io himself, while channeling. Tether can keep affecting Io's allies and provide them with healing and mana even DURING Disruption. Spirits stay active and can do damage DURING Disruption. He doesn't really have any buffs or passives to be dispelled or broken with Demonic Purge.

pairs.name: Zeus
pairs.reason: Zeus outranges and out-pokes Shadow Fiend. He doesn’t care about armor or BKB early, and constantly chips SF down. Zeus can cancel Blink Dagger from fog with his global ult.

pairs.name: Lina
pairs.reason: Lina outranges SF and can kill him before he gets BKB. Her high burst and fast right-clicks make laning and mid-game fights difficult for Shadow Fiend unless he gets the jump first.

pairs.name: Shadow Demon
pairs.reason: Shadow Demon can disrupt Shadow Fiend’s combos. He removes SF from the fight with Disruption, sets up ganks, and can use Shadow Poison to scout and cancel Blink Dagger.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: Lone Druid’s bear can break Shackles or tank Serpent Wards while the Druid focuses down Shaman. The dual-target threat makes it hard to lock him down properly in fights.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Too many illusions for Shadow Shaman to deal with. His single-target disables are ineffective against a flood of clones, and PL can easily slip past wards and isolate him.

pairs.name: Beastmaster
pairs.reason: Beastmaster’s summons cancel Shackles. Primal Roar can easily kill or disable Shadow Shaman before he casts anything. He also pushes harder and faster.

pairs.name: Abaddon
pairs.reason: Abaddon dispels Global Silence with Aphotic Shield and his ultimate, Borrowed Time, triggers despite silence. He removes Arcane Curse from himself or allies easily. Silencer has no way to stop Abaddon’s sustain-based playstyle.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Silencer struggles heavily against illusions and Naga’s Song of the Siren resets fights, making Global Silence ineffective. Naga also has natural magic resistance and multiple targets to soak Glaives. In the late game, Silencer becomes irrelevant due to illusion spam.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen doesn’t rely on spell combos in fights, so Global Silence has limited impact. His army of creeps ignores Arcane Curse, Silencer lacks wave clear and can’t pressure Chen’s push strategy.

pairs.name: Lycan
pairs.reason: Lycan’s high movement speed and summons overwhelm Skywrath. He runs Skywrath down with ease, and Skywrath’s spells don’t stop Lycan’s push. Once Lycan builds BKB, Skywrath is a non-threat.

pairs.name: Lone Druid
pairs.reason: The Spirit Bear tanks Mystic Flare and disables Skywrath with entangle. Skywrath has no control over the bear or its durability. The Druid himself can kill Sky quickly with ranged damage or Blink Bear rushes.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Skywrath wastes a full combo on Wraith King’s first life. With BKB and reincarnation, Wraith King ignores Skywrath’s control completely. He closes the gap and punishes squishy supports easily.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Dark Pact purges off Corrosive Haze quickly and can pre-cast it to remove the Slithereen Crush stun duration, which removes Slardar's key tool for chasing and bursting. Shadow Dance makes Slark untargetable, so even if he’s low, Slardar can’t finish him off during that duration.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Chaos Knight overwhelms Slardar with multiple illusions, making it hard for him to focus the real hero even with Corrosive Haze. Slardar’s single-target focus struggles against CK’s chaos and burst. CK also has high physical damage that melts Slardar before he can sustain in fights. Slardar’s armor reduction has little value when CK overwhelms him with illusion-based damage. Manta style and phantasm dispel corrosive haze.

pairs.name: Terrorblade
pairs.reason: Terrorblade is another illusion-based hero who shrugs off Slardar’s armor reduction thanks to high armor and multiple units. Once he gets Manta and Satanic, he easily outlasts Slardar in fights. Slardar has no way to clear illusions efficiently, which weakens his impact in late game. Terrorblade also punishes Slardar’s aggression with strong counter-initiation.

pairs.name: Earthshaker
pairs.reason: Despite Dark Pact being able to dispell both Aftershock and Fissure's stuns the sheer amount of constant AOE control that Earthshaker provides simply overwhelms Slark as they are able to affect him during Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Both Black Hole and Midnight Pulse can affect Slark despite his heavy defensive kit. Dark Pact does not dispel either, while Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud (Aghanim's Shard upgrade) do not prevent their effects due to them being AOE, giving Enigma a reliable way of locking down Slark . Black Hole can suck Slark back in as he Pounces and Midnight Pulse can destroy a large are of trees preventing him from hiding to heal up with Barracuda.

pairs.name: Leshrac
pairs.reason: Leshrac's abundance of AOE damage allows him to damage Slark during his core defensive mechanims - Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud. Slark's low Strength gain makes him an easy target for Lesh in the early and mid game, before Slark farms up some tanky items and often finds himself run down by Lesh.

pairs.name: Bounty Hunter
pairs.reason: Bounty Hunter snipes Snapfire in the backlines with Track and burst. He snowballs off gold from repeated kills on her. Snapfire has no escape if caught out of position. Track removes her fog safety and limits her aggressive posturing.

pairs.name: Void Spirit
pairs.reason: Void Spirit avoids her spells with Dissimilate and Astral Step. He closes gaps quickly and silences Snapfire before she casts anything. She can’t react fast enough to his mobility. Snapfire is punished hard for overextending or mispositioning.

pairs.name: Broodmother
pairs.reason: Broodmother avoids Snapfire’s AoE with Spiderlings and overwhelms her. Snapfire’s spells have long cooldowns and can’t clear full waves of spiders fast enough. Brood dominates the map and Snapfire can’t keep up in tempo. Her low mobility is a liability.

pairs.name: Centaur Warrunner
pairs.reason: Centaur Warrunner is naturally tanky, and with Blade Mail and his passive Retaliate, he can reflect a lot of Sniper’s damage. As a frequent Blink Dagger buyer, he can close the distance easily and punish Sniper. His ultimate, Stampede, helps his team initiate or escape, making him an effective counter to Sniper.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling can turn into Sniper and outdamage him with higher attack speed and agility when fully morphed. He can also chase and finish Sniper off using Waveform, making it hard for Sniper to escape or trade effectively.

pairs.name: Undying
pairs.reason: Undying is able to abuse Spectre when she's at her weakest - in the laning stage. He can constantly harass and pressure her with Decay and Rightclicks in order to disrupt her ability to secure sufficient resources in the lane, offsetting her entire game.

pairs.name: Wraith King
pairs.reason: Wraith King's innate sustain allows him to man fight Spectre as by herself she doesn't output amazing damage and the Dispersion damage she relies on is offset by WK's Lifesteal. Silver Edge, which provides Break is a naturally great pickup for WK. He's got 2 lives.

pairs.name: Dark Seer
pairs.reason: Dark Seer is able shut Spectre down in lane due to Ion Shell and offset her game entirely. What's worse is that even if Spectre ever gets to that late game where she thrives, Dark Seer is able to make multiple Illusions of her and use Spectre's strength against her and her team as Wall of Replica and Normal Punch (Aghanim's Scepter Upgrade) Illusions inherit Desolate.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Ember Spirit has an easy time dodging the Charge of Darkness collision by timing his Sleight of Fist on a cluster of units when Charge is about to connect on him. If Ember Spirit doesn't have units for Sleight of Fist around him, he can still use Sleight of Fist into Searing Chains on Spirit Breaker from range to stop the Charge mid way to stop him from getting in and out of fights. Flame Guard also absorbs damage from Spirit Breaker's spells and Greater Bash procs while jumping to Fire Remnants keeps Ember Spirit safe from ever dying.

pairs.name: Enigma
pairs.reason: Enigma's instant stun from Malefice lets him easily stop Spirit Breaker from Charging at him, or away from fights, by interrupting the spell. Spirit Breaker also has a difficult time interrupting Black Hole through Charge of Darkness or Nether Strike without getting caught in the AoE himself. Enigma's Eidolons also have high magic resistance, which keeps them safe from dying to the Charge collision.

pairs.name: Invoker
pairs.reason: Invoker has multiple ways of stopping Spirit Breaker's Charge to ensure he does not connect with his spell. Spirit Breaker can practically never cast his ultimate when affected by Cold Snap as it gets interrupted by damage instances. The slow from Ice Wall also doesn't let Spirit Breaker Charge away or into fights. Invoker's Tornado also dispels Bulldoze, which is Spirit Breaker's main survival tool.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom prevents Storm Spirit from using all of his abilities and items, rendering Storm Spirit useless in a fight.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Flame Guard absorbs up to 500 magical damage (700 with Level 10 talents), which helps Ember Spirit survive against Storm Spirit's high magical damage. Searing Chains can root enemies up to 3 seconds, making Storm Spirit unable to escape with Ball Lightning. Fire Remnant deals high magical damage when casting multiple instances at once, granting Ember Spirit the damage to burst Storm Spirit down in the early to mid game.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Berserker's Call prevents Sven from bursting his targets before Axe can interfere. The worst kind of opponent for Sven is one who can stop him from attacking who he wants to, which is exactly what Axe does. Culling Blade may finish off Sven before he has the chance to lifesteal or run with Warcry. Axe is a very common Blade Mail carrier which will make very short work of a Sven with God's Strength activated.

pairs.name: Slardar
pairs.reason: Slardar shreds Sven's high armor advantage with Corrosive Haze, turning him from a tank into a glass cannon. Slardar’s bash interrupts Sven's movement and combos, making it harder to burst down targets. Once Slardar initiates first, Sven often gets killed before even casting his ult. Vision from Haze also makes Sven’s farming patterns more predictable.

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord thrives in long, drawn-out fights, while Sven is all about quick bursts with God Strength. If Troll survives Sven’s combo, he wins the fight almost every time with his attack speed and Battle Trance. Troll also builds Basher and Satanic, making him tanky and hard to kite. Sven's stun is unreliable if Troll gets BKB first.

pairs.name: Ember Spirit
pairs.reason: Ember Spirit can easily dodge Techies' Blast Off! and Sticky Bomb by timing his Sleight of Fist on a bunch of units. Ember Spirit can also throw Fire Remnants and jump to them during Sleight of Fist to avoid exploding Proximity Mines around him. Flame Guard also provides a magic damage barrier to absorb a lot of Techies' damage from his spells. Ember Spirit can also deal damage from range with his Sleight of Fist into Searing Chains combo to avoid running into Proximity Mines.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Juggernaut's Blade Fury provides massive magic resistance during the spin to mitigate most of Techies' high damage from Sticky Bomb, Blast Off!, and Proximity Mines. The Blade Fury debuff immunity also avoids the Blast Off! stun, while the dispel takes off the Reactive Tazer disarm. Juggernaut can also Omnislash and Swiftslash Techies during his Blast Off! jump to turn the fight. Healing Ward is also great at healing up Juggernaut and his entire team to counteract Techies' heavy AoE damage.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer's Rage provides massive magic resistance during the spell to mitigate most of Techies' high damage from Sticky Bomb, Blast Off!, and Proximity Mines. The Rage debuff immunity also avoids the Blast Off! stun, while the dispel takes off the Reactive Tazer disarm. Rage is particularly effective at soaking multiple Proximity Mines while taking very little damage.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Phantom Lancer's illusions destroy Refraction charges very quickly. Diffusal Blade, his core item, drains Templar Assassin's small mana pool, rendering her unable to save herself with Meld.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga’s illusions burn through Refraction instantly, removing TA's key defense. Templar Assassin struggles to clear illusions efficiently and gets overwhelmed in prolonged fights. Song of the Siren can reset fights or catch TA before she gets a kill.

pairs.name: Batrider
pairs.reason: Sticky Napalm ruins her mobility and melts Refraction charges rapidly. Flaming Lasso completely removes her from fights, especially pre-BKB. Batrider also breaks Meld positioning and traps with Firefly vision.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: PL overwhelms TB with illusions. TB can't tell the real PL apart, and Reflection isn’t useful against illusions. PL also has natural Diffusal Blade to burn TB’s mana, making Sunder risky or impossible to use.

pairs.name: Tinker
pairs.reason: Tinker spams lasers to wipe illusions from afar. TB can’t reach or pressure him easily without support, and Laser's Blind heavily cripples TB’s right-click DPS. Tinker thrives against illusion carries like TB.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Winter’s Curse can turn TB’s illusions against him, dealing massive damage to his teammates. She stalls pushes with Splinter Blast and zones TB out with Arctic Burn. Wyvern punishes TB's clumping and illusions.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: Dark Pact dispels debuffs from Gush, Anchor Smash and even Ravage if timed correctly. Kraken Shell cannot restore attributes stolen by Essence Shift or dispel the leash if he gets Pounced.

pairs.name: Witch Doctor
pairs.reason: Maledict is highly effective against tanky heroes like Tidehunter and can help burst him down in lane. Additionally, Witch Doctor’s Death Ward deals pure damage, which cannot be mitigated by Kraken Shell

pairs.name: Outworld Destroyer
pairs.reason: Outworld Devourer’s Arcane Orb deals pure damage, bypassing Kraken Shell. His ultimate can burst Tidehunter due to Tide’s relatively low mana pool, and Astral Imprisonment can save allies from Ravage, making him a tough matchup

pairs.name: Faceless Void
pairs.reason: Chronosphere traps Timbersaw before he can react with Timber Chain. Timbersaw cannot save allies or himself inside the sphere. Faceless Void's physical burst bypasses his reactive armor. He’s especially vulnerable if caught without mana or Chain cooldown.

pairs.name: Pugna
pairs.reason: Pugna’s Nether Ward punishes Timbersaw’s high spell frequency. Decrepify interrupts Chakram burst and saves teammates. Life Drain cuts through Timbersaw’s defenses and regrowth. Pugna makes Timbersaw’s damage and durability unreliable in teamfights.

pairs.name: Grimstroke
pairs.reason: Soulbind prevents double Timber Chains or escaping with mobility. Ink Swell stuns him if he stays in close quarters. Grimstroke punishes Timbersaw’s grouped aggression. His combo disables even tanky targets long enough for allies to finish them off.

pairs.name: Clockwerk
pairs.reason: Clockwerk's Rocket Flare gives him vision to find Tinker hiding in tree lines, which lets him follow up with his long range Hookshot to lock down Tinker and interrupt his Rearm and Keen Conveyance teleport. Battery Assault also prevents Tinker from Rearming or teleporting, while Defense Matrix does little against the mini stun inside Power Cogs. Clockwerk can also kick one of his Power Cogs from range to stop Tinker's channeling spells.

pairs.name: Doom
pairs.reason: Doom's ultimate Doom disables a squishy and immobile Tinker from using spells, which makes him completely useless as he relies heavily on his spells to get in and out of fights as well as do damage and survive. Doom can easily run down Tinker in the duration of his ultimate with the movement speed boost during Scorched Earth. The Infernal Blade mini stun also stops Tinker's channeling spells.

pairs.name: Earth Spirit
pairs.reason: Earth Spirit's Rolling Boulder lets him get on top of a squishy and immobile Tinker from range to follow up with the damage and control from the rest of his spells to burst him down. Earth Spirit is also invulnerable during his Roll, letting him avoid the March of the Machines damage. The Geomagnetic Grip silence also interrupts Tinker's channeling spells, including his Keen Conveyance teleport.

pairs.name: Necrophos
pairs.reason: Necrophos shrugs off Tiny’s burst with sustain and Ghost Shroud. Reaper’s Scythe punishes Tiny’s low status resistance early. Avalanche and Toss do little once Necrophos is tanky. He scales better and punishes Tiny’s lack of BKB early.

pairs.name: Enchantress
pairs.reason: Enchantress survives early burst with Untouchable and heal. Tiny cannot deal enough right-click damage to finish her off. Nature’s Attendants keeps her alive through Avalanche Toss. She dominates long fights where Tiny runs out of impact.

pairs.name: Undying
pairs.reason: Undying’s zombies and Tombstone make it hard for Tiny to engage. Decay reduces Tiny’s damage and survivability. Tiny’s burst is wasted on tanky targets like Undying who soaks up spell combos that would otherwise kill squishies heroes.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Tidehunters Kraken Shell removes all your debuffs at a certain threshold which makes Treant less useful in the mid to late game.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen floods the map with creeps, bypassing Living Armor’s value through constant pressure. He outheals or dispels Treant’s chip damage, and his Hand of God negates Leech Seed damage completely.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Naga pushes multiple lanes and illusions burn through Living Armor fast. Song of the Siren resets any Overgrowth initiation, wasting Treant's major cooldown. Treant struggles to clear illusions or find the real Naga.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Cold Embrace can protect Troll Warlord's target, especially during Battle Trance. Winter's Curse can turn Troll Warlord's high physical damage and attack speed against his allies.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord is bad against Axe because Axe's Berserker's Call forces Troll Warlord to attack him during his ultimate, which allows Axe to lock him down and kill him easily with Blade Mail and Culling Blade. Troll Warlord's reliance on right-clicking makes him vulnerable to the counterattack mechanic of Axe, especially during the laning and early mid-game phase. Troll Warlord cannot out-sustain the pure disable and burst Axe brings with his spell combo.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord struggles against Naga Siren because her illusions overwhelm him and make it difficult to focus the real hero during fights. Ensnare prevents Troll Warlord from repositioning or escaping, especially when he’s channeling Battle Trance. Naga Siren's Song of the Siren can reset fights or waste Troll Warlord’s ultimate duration. The illusion spam and evasion from Manta Style or Butterfly also weaken Troll Warlord’s impact in late-game duels.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Mana Break is very effective against Tusk, as he has a very low mana pool. Blink allows Anti-Mage to escape from an incoming Snowball.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Lifestealer has multiple ways of dispelling both Pit of Malice and Firestorm trough Rage/Unfettered and Infest. Infest can be used during Pit of Malice's root and Rage negates Atrophy Aura's damage reduction for it's duration. Being a tank shredder Lifestealer naturally matches up well versus Underlord as he has ample sustain trough Open Wounds, Infest and Feast.

pairs.name: Juggernaut
pairs.reason: Blade Fury can dispel both Pit of Malice and Firestorm. Healing Ward provides Jugg and his team with AOE healing to counteract Underlords AOE damage. Omnislash and Swiftslash (Jugg's Aghanim's Scepter) can be used during Pit of Malice's root and dispel him, while not being affected by Atrophy Aura for their duration.

pairs.name: Huskar
pairs.reason: Berserker's Blood provides Huskar with Magic Resistance to mitigate the damage from Firestorm and ample sustain to counteract it's DOT effect. Life Break can be used during Pit of Malice to dispel the root and leave it's AOE altogether.

pairs.name: Snapfire
pairs.reason: Lil' Shredder destroys Tombstone quickly from a safe range. Her high magic burst punishes Undying's low mobility and poor scaling. She also zones Undying out of teamfights and punishes his early grouping.

pairs.name: Jakiro
pairs.reason: Jakiro attacks twice so he can easily destroy tombstone. Ice Path and Dual Breath interrupt Tombstone fights and slow Undying’s early aggression. His long-range spell makes Undying’s push ineffective.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Zombies barely affect Medusa due to her Split Shot and high effective mana pool. Stone Gaze disables Undying and forces him out of position if he commits early. She simply outscales and ignores his impact in long fights.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Ursa has no way to clear illusions quickly, making him vulnerable to Chaos Bolt and Phantasm combo. Reality Rift can quickly relocate or reinitiate on Ursa once the duration of Enrage is over. Phantasm can be used to dispel Earthshock's slow. Manta Style is another item that counter Ursa greatly. Ursa has low mobility, once jumped on by Reality Rift, Ursa struggles to escape. Doom

pairs.name: Troll Warlord
pairs.reason: Troll Warlord can be a tough matchup for Ursa. Whirling Axes apply miss chance, making it difficult for Ursa to land attacks and build Fury Swipes stacks. If Ursa initiates first, Troll can activate Battle Trance and potentially outlast Ursa in a drawn-out manfight.

pairs.name: Winter Wyvern
pairs.reason: Cold Embrace completely negates Ursa’s physical damage while healing the target, shutting down his burst potential. Winter’s Curse can also turn Ursa’s high attack speed and damage against his own team, often causing him to burst down an ally

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: Elder Titan removes base armor with Natural Order, making Venge and her illusions extremely vulnerable. His stun and stomp combo disable her before she casts. ET’s AoE zoning keeps her away from her ideal positioning. Venge becomes fragile in fights.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Brew’s Primal Split ruins Venge’s coordination and prevents focus fire. He can cyclone Venge or her carry during Swap attempts. Brew’s survivability means her armor reduction has less value. Venge can’t stop him once he splits.

pairs.name: Terrorblade
pairs.reason: Terrorblade shrugs off armor debuffs with high stats and illusions. Venge can’t disable him long enough to prevent Sunder. His illusions melt her with right clicks. Swap doesn’t remove his massive damage presence from the fight.

pairs.name: Brewmaster
pairs.reason: Brewmaster dispels all of Venomancer’s damage-over-time effects with Primal Split. During the split, he removes Plague Wards and disables Venomancer’s positioning. Gale and Nova become useless once dispelled. Brewmaster’s utility and tankiness outlasts Venomancer’s slow burn.

pairs.name: Storm Spirit
pairs.reason: Storm Spirit zips in and out of fights, ignoring all of Venomancer’s slow-based control. He can burst Venomancer before poison becomes a threat. Venomancer lacks disables to lock Storm down. Once behind, he can’t recover against Storm’s map pressure.

pairs.name: Tinker
pairs.reason: Tinker has the range and burst to kill Venomancer without getting close. Venomancer’s slow poison damage is too slow to pressure Tinker’s farming pace. Tinker’s mobility keeps him out of reach.

pairs.name: Terrorblade
pairs.reason: Terrorblade resists Viper's early pressure due to high armor and Conjure Image. He outscales Viper and punishes his lack of burst. Viper can’t stop Sunder and gets destroyed in later fights. TB's illusions also act as meat shields against Viper's output.

pairs.name: Arc Warden
pairs.reason: Arc Warden outranges Viper with Spark Wraith zoning and Tempest Double. He controls space safely while Viper struggles to close the gap. His clone soaks Viper's abilities and allows for free harassment. Arc Warden wins the map with split pressure.

pairs.name: Chaos Knight
pairs.reason: Chaos Knight overpowers Viper with illusions and high burst damage. Viper’s slow single-target spells don’t impact CK’s phantoms. He forces Viper to buy items like Mjollnir that delay timing. CK punishes Viper's immobility and paper armor.

pairs.name: Tidehunter
pairs.reason: Visage's Familiars cannot penetrate Kraken Shell and will do almost no damage to Tidehunter. Anchor Smash's bonus damage has the potential to kill Familiars or reduce their damage.

pairs.name: Naga Siren
pairs.reason: Visage is bad against Naga Siren because her illusions overwhelm Visage and make it hard for him to identify and focus the real target. Her Song of the Siren resets fights and completely wastes Visage’s burst timing with Familiars. Naga’s illusions soak up Soul Assumption charges, denying burst potential. Over time, her Radiance and Diffusal Blade combo also burns Visage’s mana and weakens his survivability.

pairs.name: Phantom Lancer
pairs.reason: Visage is bad against Phantom Lancer because the massive number of illusions confuse Visage’s auto-targeting from Familiars and force Soul Assumption onto the wrong units. Phantom Lancer is hard to catch due to Doppelganger and high agility scaling, while Visage lacks reliable area-of-effect damage to clear illusions. Once Phantom Lancer builds Manta Style and Heart, he becomes unkillable for Visage. The birds also lose effectiveness against dispersed illusions.

pairs.name: Chen
pairs.reason: Chen’s summons tank Void Spirit’s burst and make pickoffs harder. Divine Favor and Hand of God keep allies alive after being engaged on. Chen’s early push punishes Void Spirit’s slow wave clear. Void Spirit has trouble fighting multiple creeps and heals

pairs.name: Night Stalker
pairs.reason: Night Stalker silences and sticks to Void Spirit during nighttime. Void Spirit can't escape easily with Void and Crippling Fear. Once BKB is online, Night Stalker becomes unkillable for him. Void Spirit needs defensive items to survive early ganks.

pairs.name: Monkey King
pairs.reason: Monkey King controls Void Spirit with Jingu and Boundless Strike. Void Spirit can’t freely move inside Wukong’s Command. He loses lane trades and gets zoned in fights. Monkey punishes missed steps with burst and lifesteal.

pairs.name: Elder Titan
pairs.reason: ET negates Warlock’s sustain by reducing magic resistance. His spirit combo and Echo Stomp can zone Warlock and stop his channeled abilities. Bonds are useless if Warlock dies before casting.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling's mobility and sustain shrug off Bonds and Upheaval. He quickly kills Warlock in the backline and survives Mystic Flare-level bursts. Warlock has no way to lock Morphling down.

pairs.name: Bristleback
pairs.reason: Bristle thrives in long fights and shrugs off Warlock's harassment. Fatal Bonds doesn't deter him, and Golems do little unless the whole team commits. He’s too tanky for Warlock to influence meaningfully.

pairs.name: Morphling
pairs.reason: Morphling outscales Weaver and can morph into him for mobility. Weaver has no way to burst Morphling before he shifts to strength. Morphling’s sustain and magic burst punish Weaver's low HP. In late game, Morphling wins almost every duel.

pairs.name: Puck
pairs.reason: Puck’s silence and Dream Coil both counter Weaver’s escape tools. Weaver struggles to hit moving targets with Puck’s evasive playstyle. Puck also scales better into midgame utility. Coil forces Weaver into risky fights without his ult.

pairs.name: Rubick
pairs.reason: Rubick can steal Time Lapse or Shukuchi and turn them against Weaver. His lift disables Weaver long enough to kill him. Rubick builds survivability and utility faster. A good Rubick makes Weaver’s mobility a liability.

pairs.name: Axe
pairs.reason: Windranger’s long channeling Focus Fire makes her a prime target for Berserker’s Call. Axe forces her to attack him, triggering counter helix and controlling her. She gets countered hard during her burst window.

pairs.name: Tiny
pairs.reason: Tiny can burst Windranger instantly with Avalanche and Toss combo. Her Windrun does nothing to stop his magic burst and toss disables her mobility. She has trouble locking him down before he deletes her. He invalidates her midgame power spikes with his quick burst.

pairs.name: Queen of Pain
pairs.reason: Queen of Pain bursts Windranger down with Scream and Sonic Wave before she can Windrun. Her mobility allows her to escape Focus Fire and avoid Shackleshot setups. Windranger can’t contest her laning pressure or match her tempo. Queen of Pain thrives against squishy mids like her.

pairs.name: Pugna
pairs.reason: Pugna's Nether Ward punishes Winter Wyvern for casting spells by dealing damage, making her abilities costly to use. Additionally, Decrepify can save the target of Winter's Curse by making them immune to physical damage

pairs.name: Outworld Destroyer
pairs.reason: Outworld Devourer can counter Winter’s Curse by using Astral Imprisonment to save allies. His magical damage also bypasses Cold Embrace, making Wyvern’s primary save much less effective

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage is a strong counter to Winter Wyvern due to his high magic resistance and spell reflection from Counterspell. His mobility with Blink and Manta Style makes it hard for Wyvern to escape or react defensively before being killed .If he successfully reflects Winter’s Curse, he can potentially turn the entire fight in his favor

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage can easily deflect your predictable Paralyzing Cask and set you up for a kill, in addition he can blink away from trouble or blink in pre-emptively with Counter Spell.

pairs.name: Medusa
pairs.reason: Her Mana Shield makes her hard to kill with Death Ward or Maledict. She also outlasts long fights where Witch Doctor is most dangerous.

pairs.name: Pangolier
pairs.reason: Constant mobility and spell immunity during Rolling Thunder make it hard for Witch Doctor to channel Death Ward or land Cask and Maledict effectively.

pairs.name: Phoenix
pairs.reason: WK's total damage output comes mostly from his attacks and Phoenix can make them both miss with Blinding Sun or reduce their frequency with Fire Spirits. Supernova can be hard for WK to deal with as he is a melee hero and also lacks good base attack speed or built in debuff immunity.

pairs.name: Slark
pairs.reason: WK's total damage output comes mostly from his attacks, which he cannot take advantage of during Slark's main defensive tools: Shadow Dance and Depth Shroud (Aghanim's Shard upgrade). Dark Pact can dispel Wraithfire Blast and Reincarnation's Wraith form still provides Slark with Essence Shift stacks.

pairs.name: Lifestealer
pairs.reason: Rage/Unfettered can be used to dodge/dispel Wraithfire Blast. Feast + Open Wounds outheal Vampiric Spirit and in a 1 on 1 fight, which WK is supposedly "king" of LS tends to win as he outdamages and outheals WK. Infest can disarm trough Debuff Immunity once upgraded with Aghanim's Scepter, removing most of WK's damage output for it's duration.

pairs.name: Broodmother
pairs.reason: Broodmother’s webs let her sustain against Zeus’s nukes by providing regeneration and damage reduction. Her mobility in the webs also allows her to chase down Zeus easily, making it hard for him to escape.

pairs.name: Anti-Mage
pairs.reason: Anti-Mage’s built-in magic resistance reduces Zeus’s damage, making it harder for him to burst AM down. Additionally, Anti-Mage can reflect Zeus’s spells with Counterspell and quickly kill him using Mana Void when Zeus’s mana is low.

pairs.name: Void Spirit
pairs.reason: Void Spirit can quickly close the gap on Zeus and burst him down. His Resonant Pulse allows him to block incoming magic damage, reducing Zeus’s burst effectiveness and giving him an edge in fights.
